title: Reduce console backend fanout and optimize resolver hydration for lower tail latency
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Background:
The Console backend is experiencing increased p95/p99 latency on composite API endpoints that fan out to multiple services and GraphQL resolvers. Root causes we've observed: duplicated resolver calls across sibling fields, fragmented cache keys, redundant DB/API fetches within a single request, and heavy JSON serialization of large payloads. These issues exacerbate tail latency during bursts and degrade customer experience for dashboards and rollouts pages.

Goal:
Reduce end-to-end p95 and p99 latency for Console product list/detail endpoints by 25%-40% in steady-state and during mid-size bursts (10-50 reqs/s). Improve CPU and memory efficiency for the backend by consolidating fetch paths and avoiding repeated work per request.

Scope / In-scope:
- Add a per-request coalescing layer in the Console backend HTTP handler to deduplicate identical downstream fetches (DB, internal HTTP to aggregator services, and GraphQL data sources).
- Implement a lightweight in-request cache/registry used by resolvers to short-circuit duplicate calls and reuse in-flight promises.
- Introduce field projection hints from GraphQL resolvers to the fetch layer to avoid overfetch (only request fields necessary for the response).
- Rework two heavy endpoints (route: /console/projects and /console/rollouts/:id) to use the new coalescing path and streaming hydration for large lists.
- Add metrics (per-request dedupe count, cache hit rate, serialization time) and Grafana dashboard panels for rollout.

Out-of-scope (for this ticket):
- Large DB schema changes or introducing a centralized caching tier (Redis) — those are follow-ups if needed.
- Client-side changes to reduce payloads.

Acceptance criteria:
- p95 latency of /console/projects reduced by >= 30% on staging load test (baseline attached).
- p99 latency of /console/rollouts/:id reduced by >= 25% on the same load test.
- Metrics emitted for dedupe_count and in_request_cache_hit_rate with dashboards linked.
- No increase in error rate or CPU OOMs during canary traffic (0 -> 5% -> 25% rollout stages).
- PRs reviewed and merged with green CI and e2e smoke on staging.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design: small RFC in Confluence describing coalescer API, lifecycle, and failure semantics. Include patterns for resolver integration and projection hints. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Console+Coalescer+RFC
2) Implement a middleware in the HTTP layer that attaches a RequestRegistry to the request context. The registry stores in-flight promises keyed by a stable fetch key and small serialized args.
3) Wrap existing data-source functions (DB fetch, internal HTTP clients) with a thin dedupe wrapper that consults RequestRegistry. Add feature flag to toggle on staging per-route.
4) Add resolver helpers: useRegistryFetch(key, fetchFn, projectionFields) — fetchFn receives projection hints. Replace hot resolvers in projects and rollouts endpoints to call this helper.
5) Add lightweight projection logic to the fetch layer: translate resolver field requirements to selected columns or query params where source supports it. Fall back to full fetch when projection unsupported.
6) Introduce streaming hydration for project list: send initial minimal list and stream per-item details asynchronously (configurable via header).
7) Add metrics, tracing spans, and logging for dedupe events and serialization durations.
8) Canary rollout: feature-flag first on staging, run load tests (k6 scripts), then canary 5% in prod, monitor dashboards, then 25%, then full.

Tasks (checkbox-style list to track work):
- [x] RFC + design doc (Confluence) by 2026-02-23 (Aisha)
- [x] Prototype in local dev: RequestRegistry & dedupe wrapper (branch: feat/console-coalescer-proto)
- [ ] Implement registry as middleware and passthrough types (PR: GH#6287)
- [ ] Wrap DB and internal HTTP clients with registry-aware adapters (PR: GH#6292)
- [ ] Modify hot resolvers for projects and rollouts to use useRegistryFetch (PR: GH#6301)
- [ ] Add projection hint plumbing to fetch layer (PR: GH#6310)
- [ ] Instrument metrics/tracing and add Grafana panels (dash: D-950)
- [ ] Write e2e smoke and k6 load scripts for regression verification (PR: GH#6325)
- [ ] Canary rollout and monitor (Ops runbook updated)

Progress updates and decisions (chronological):
- 2026-02-22 — Aisha: RFC posted. Primary design decision: in-request registry only (no cross-request coordination) to keep risk low and avoid new infra. Opted for promise coalescing to support in-flight dedupe.
- 2026-02-25 — Marcelo: Prototype shows 35% p95 improvement on local emulation for /console/projects when dedupe reduces duplicate DB calls. Trade-off: added ~100 bytes per request context. Acceptable.
- 2026-03-01 — Review (PM + Design): PM Lina Park asked to ensure streaming path preserves existing UI UX (loading indicators). Design approved placeholder skeleton. Action: add header opt-in for streaming hydration.
- 2026-03-04 — Security review: quick sync with Security lead (Tom Nguyen). No sensitive data is persisted in registry; registry lives in-process and cleared at request end. Security -> no additional controls required.
- 2026-03-08 — Engineering review: PRs GH#6287 and GH#6292 opened. Initial feedback: prefer explicit stable fetch key generation helpers to avoid accidental collisions across different fetch functions. Marcelo to add utility and unit tests.

Review feedback and follow-ups:
- Ensure fetch key includes source name, projection fingerprint, and version tag (e.g., fetchKey = `projects:byId:v2:${id}:${projHash}`). Avoid string concatenation pitfalls — use a small deterministic serializer.
- Add integration test asserting that two concurrent resolvers calling the same underlying data-source only trigger one backend call (use nock for HTTP and test DB spy).
- Add TTL for in-request cache entries equal to request lifetime; protect registry from being used outside of request lifecycle.

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: subtle behavioral changes if projection hints are incorrect -> data mismatch. Mitigation: projection is advisory — fetch layer will fall back to full fetch if required fields missing. Add per-route unit tests.
- Risk: accidental growth of in-request registry causing memory pressure on high concurrency. Mitigation: cap number of registry entries per request (configurable, default 100). Log and short-circuit when exceeded.

Monitoring and observability:
- Emit metrics: console.coalescer.dedupe_count (counter), console.coalescer.in_request_cache_hit_rate (gauge), console.serialization.duration_ms (histogram).
- Dashboard panels: dedupe_rate, hit_rate, p95/p99 before & after, serialization time distribution. Dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/console-performance/console-coalescer

Rollout plan:
- Staging toggle on for 100% traffic, run load tests and verify acceptance criteria.
- Prod: feature flag -> 5% traffic for 24h, monitor; if green -> 25% for 48h; if green -> 100%.
- Full rollback plan: disable flag and revert configs, rollback PR if regressions detected.

Notes for assignee (Marcelo):
- Start by landing the RequestRegistry middleware and the dedupe wrapper for internal HTTP clients — these are the lowest-risk changes that unlock the rest.
- Add unit tests for stable fetch key helper and integration test for concurrent dedupe.
- Coordinate with Lina (PM) to ensure streaming UI header is compatible with front-end rollout (Lina Park: lina@redwood.ai).
